values.DataCenterNotes: The Wisconsin commission case page for the Paris engine plant places the seven gas engines, up to 128 megawatts, at the Lakeshore Capacity Improvement Project regulator station in the Town of Paris, which is the end of the Lakeshore Lateral. A Milwaukee public radio report on the May 2025 commission approval of the Paris and Oak Creek plants says We Energies points to a Microsoft data center being built in Racine County, and one commissioner cited data centers in southeastern Wisconsin as a reason for his vote.

verifications.note: Case page for the Paris engine plant. Puts the plant at the Lakeshore Capacity Improvement Project regulator station in the Town of Paris. Does not mention data centers.
Says We Energies points to a Microsoft data center in Racine County as a reason for the plants, and a commissioner cited data centers. Does not name the Lakeshore pipeline.

records.researcher_notes: The Lakeshore Lateral was approved in 2020 and built in 2021 for regional demand, so it was not planned for the data center. It now ends at the site of the new Paris engine plant, which We Energies and the commission tied to the Microsoft data center in Mount Pleasant. The link between the pipeline and the plant rests on the plant being sited at the Lakeshore regulator station. No page says in one sentence that the lateral feeds the plant, so please review. The pipeline source and the data center source are different pages.

ledger.note: The Paris engine plant is sited at the Lakeshore regulator station at the end of the lateral. We Energies and a commissioner tied the Paris and Oak Creek plants to the Microsoft data center in Racine County. No page states outright that the lateral feeds the plant, so this is an inferred link.
